text:
Oscar Chen: Heads-up — I'm seeing weird invoice lines for a few customers: when they hit per-minute rate limits they end up with either 0-token or negative token adjustments on the invoice. Not sure if it's a pipeline bug or a routing quirk.
Maria Gomez: Hmm — do you have a concrete example (req id + raw events)?
Oscar Chen: Yep. Here's a raw ingest event sample we captured from the proxy:
```
{
  \"req_id\": \"abc123\",
  \"user_id\": \"acct_42\",
  \"status\": 429,
  \"reported_tokens\": 0,
  \"model\": \"redwood/gpt-4o\",
  \"route\": \"burst\",
  \"timestamp\": 1670000000
}
```
Oscar Chen: But later in the billing join we get an estimated_tokens = 512 attributed to the same req_id. So invoice shows an adjustment like -512 then +512 on next line, or sometimes just a 0 net but odd negative lines.
Jun Park: That's consistent with a race between the proxy rejection and the post-hoc estimator in the \"token-estimate\" microservice. If the estimator runs after ingest it may write estimated_tokens even for 429s.
metering-bot: ingest-service: event abc123 received (status=429) -> enqueued to raw-usage, trace_id=tx-9876
Product QA: Noted this shows up in staging invoices too when we push noisy canary traffic.
Maria Gomez: Do we already filter by status in the billing join? I thought we only join on req_id and sum(tokens).
Oscar Chen: Current ingestion schema:
```
usage_events(req_id, user_id, status, reported_tokens, estimated_tokens, ts)
```
and billing query is roughly:
```
INSERT INTO invoice_lines
SELECT user_id, sum(coalesce(reported_tokens, estimated_tokens)) as tokens
FROM usage_events
WHERE invoice_period = '2026-02'
GROUP BY user_id;
```
Jun Park: There's the bug: `coalesce(reported_tokens, estimated_tokens)` will pick estimated_tokens when reported_tokens==0 (which is valid for 429). We need a rule: only use estimated_tokens when status < 400 OR when reported_tokens is null and status < 500? (we should decide exact policy)
Maria Gomez: Agree. We probably want: use reported_tokens if reported_tokens > 0, else if status in [200..399] use estimated_tokens, else count 0. That prevents counting estimates for rejects.
Oscar Chen: I can prototype a fix in the billing SQL: `sum(case when reported_tokens > 0 then reported_tokens when status between 200 and 399 then estimated_tokens else 0 end)`
Jun Park: Also consider that some proxies send reported_tokens=0 for legitimate 0-token responses (e.g., emb endpoint). We should attach `api_method` and `model_family` in the rule to avoid overblocking.
Product QA: From a UX/invoice perspective we want idempotent lines per req_id so downstream accounting doesn't flip-flop on replays.
Maria Gomez: We should also add an invariant check in the pipeline that flags if the same req_id has both status>=400 and a non-zero tokens claim. That will help alert these cases early.
Oscar Chen: I'll open two PRs: (1) ingestion validation: drop/mark estimated_tokens when status >= 400 and reported_tokens == 0; (2) billing aggregation change to the `case when` rule so any missed events are safe.
Oscar Chen: Draft SQL for (1):
```
UPDATE usage_events
SET estimated_tokens = 0, note = 'rejected_request_no_tokens'
WHERE status >= 400 AND reported_tokens = 0 AND estimated_tokens > 0 AND ts > 1670000000;
```
Jun Park: For long term we should shift to a canonical event shape where token attribution is a separate, append-only table written only by a single service (estimator) that must include `reason` and `confidence`. That avoids joins that cause these races.
metering-bot: deploy-bot: canary deploy scheduled for token-estimator v1.3 at 2026-03-12T21:00Z
Maria Gomez: Action items:
- Oscar: open PRs for ingestion validation + billing-sql (priority P1)
- Jun: design spec for canonical token-attribution table (sync by EOD Fri)
- Product QA: add invoice regression test (staging) covering 429 + estimator replays
Product QA: tagging test cases in the invoice suite.
Oscar Chen: I've opened PR #4123 (ingestion validation) and PR #4124 (billing-aggregation). pinging @Jun Park for review.
Jun Park: Reviewing now. If tests pass I can merge and coordinate a canary of the billing job.
Maria Gomez: Thanks — please also add a dashboard card to our billing console showing `count(req_id) where status>=400 and estimated_tokens>0` so ops can monitor.
Oscar Chen: Will do. Thanks all :thumbsup:
